name: Jaw implants

card.summary: Implants placed along the angle and body of the lower jaw to widen or define it; used in facial gender surgery and cosmetic work, with little outcome research behind the forum hype.
card.aka: mandible angle implants, gonial angle implants, jawline implants
card.note: Published outcome research is limited; users and reviews raise questions about design, size and how natural the result looks.

quick.overview:
Jaw implants, sometimes called mandibular angle or gonial implants, are solid shapes of silicone, porous polyethylene or PEEK placed over the lower jawbone to add width or definition at the angle and body of the jaw. In published literature they appear mainly in facial gender-affirming surgery, where augmentation of the mandibular angle and body is described as a masculinising option.

In looksmaxxing communities they are discussed as an alternative to bimax and genioplasty, with arguments about implant design, size, body fat and how natural the result looks. Outcome research on cosmetic jaw implants is thin.
quick.mechanism: An implant is placed against the bone through an incision, usually inside the mouth, and sits under the soft tissue so that the lower face contour looks wider or squarer. Some designs are custom-made from CT scans.
quick.risks: Reported concerns include a bloated or unnatural look when implants are too large or the underlying structure is mismatched, soft-tissue sagging after removal, infection and displacement, though complications are described as minimal in one gender-affirming surgery review. Outcome data are limited.

lead: Jaw implants are alloplastic (manufactured) implants placed over the angle and body of the mandible to increase width and definition; they are also called mandibular angle or gonial angle implants.[1] A review of lower jaw contouring in facial gender-affirming surgery describes augmentation of the mandibular angle, body and chin with alloplastic implants, fat or bone as a masculinising option and reports that complications are minimal, while stating that more research on outcomes is needed.[1]

Few studies examine cosmetic jaw implants specifically. A retrospective CT study of cosmetic surgery foreign bodies in the maxillofacial region documented the imaging appearance of such materials as incidental findings, without describing implant outcomes.[2]
On looksmax.org, jaw implants are debated as an alternative or complement to bone surgery such as bimax, with questions on sizing, leanness and whether the underlying structure suits an implant.[3]

paras: In facial gender-affirming surgery, lower jaw contouring is used to harmonise the face, with reduction of the mandibular angle, body and chin for feminisation and augmentation with implants, fat or bone for masculinisation.[1] Cosmetic jaw implants outside that setting are mentioned mainly in forum and surgeon material rather than in the clinical literature.[3]

Chin implants are a related and better-documented category; materials for them include silicone, porous polyethylene and ePTFE, each with different tendencies for shifting, tissue ingrowth and difficulty of removal.[4]

No studies found on cosmetic jaw implants in the sources reviewed. Related research includes a review of lower jaw recontouring in facial gender-affirming surgery, which concluded that complications are minimal and that further research on outcomes is needed,[1] and a CT study of cosmetic foreign bodies in the maxillofacial region.[2] Studies of dental or subperiosteal jaw implants concern tooth replacement and are a separate field.

Users on looksmax.org argue about whether jaw implants look unnatural because of design or because of oversizing, with some saying results depend on how conservative the change is.[3] A separate thread asks whether being heavier at the time of surgery affects the final look and whether leaning down later solves it; replies state that a short or recessed mandible can make an implant on the side look bloated.[3]

lore.intro: Jaw implants are discussed on forums as a way to widen or define the lower face, with debates on design versus size and on which anatomy suits an implant.[3]

claims.claim: Being a little overweight at the time of surgery does not change the final implant result once weight is lost.
claims.believers: A poster asks whether the effect of body fat is temporary and replies argue that a small amount of extra fat does not change the end result.[3]
claims.experts: No published studies were identified that examine body fat and cosmetic jaw implant appearance.

claims.claim: Jaw implants look bloated or unnatural on people with a short or recessed mandible.
claims.believers: A reply in the thread says that if the mandible is short or recessed, adding material at the side can look unnatural, like being fat.[3]
claims.experts: No published trial has compared implant and bone-based jaw changes for appearance; a review of gender-affirming jaw contouring says outcome research is still needed.[1]
